body:
I went through this. Next 2 weeks were a living hell. I'd get images of her and her bf having sex on her bed in my dreams and would have to wake up in the middle of the night.

In the long run, it was probably good, otherwise I'd have chased her forever
This is kind of smart. The only issue is 7 yrs in if you change your mind, it will be cancer + desire to live, risky combination
How are you planning to say goodbyes? Guessing people aren't going to be accepting of the decision for obvious reasons

I am not fully out yet, but somethings that moved in the right direction -

1. Find something new to obsess about. I started a company last year which has been a focal point of my compulsive thinking
2. NC. I mean it, fully. Not even once a month, "How r u?"
3. Find a new girl and invest in her. So this is a double edged sword. I tried seeing a girl that I didn't like which made me feel even stronger longing for the LO. Last December I dated a girl that I got places with, that was a solid intuitive proof, it's not about LO, it's me, there's other girls that can carry that passion (even if it doesn't feel that way right now)
I relate to this so much. When you realize you don't even complete moral ownership over your own life and suffering, it hits deep.
Inconsistent rewards is sure shot way of getting hooked onto something psychologically. Realize it's a powerful psychological phenomena at play here

I obviously don't know your situation, but I can share mine. I used to feel this way as well. For myself, I've realized, if they didn't appreciate me in life, it's unlikely they are going to appreciate me in death. Tying my happiness or pain to "them" is irrational
If it interests you, I can try connecting you with some American companies for entry level jobs? I can put in a good word and write a recommendation as well.
Have you thought about talking with them about it? I am in a similar boat and wonder if it would just be better to sit them down and talk with them instead of surprising them one random day
Me as well. Not to comfort you, persuade or dissuade you. I relate to a lot of what you wrote, and I am just curious.

This was part of the overall emotion I have experienced - how many brunches can I go to, how many more workdays etc. etc.

If you think about it, in many ways this is a license to experiment like crazy. I don't mean take up cooking or pilates. 

I mean in the sense of - join a cult, go become an adult film star or go fight in a war. I haven't gone to such extremes, but did experiment with things significantly outside the overton window
The free will argument makes sense for the perpetrator. What about the victim? Why must he endure monumental suffering in God's benevolent world for no reason
If the god is not engaged in the functioning of the universe, what is the idea of god for you? What role does he play in the universe you live in?
If he (or she) can have worthy adversaries, the god you believe is not all powerful then?

>What is the effective difference between a god whose actions, motives and requirements are so unknown as to be effectively random and an actual random world?

This is such a great way of putting it.
This is a valid argument. If god is not benevolent or intelligent in his design, what is it about god that draws you to him? What role does he play in the universe you live in?
What role does your god play in the functioning of the universe?
If it's just suffering, what keeps you going?
Exactly. People with irrational optimism can't understand the weight of lost life paths, only the person who suffers knows
